title: Nova, et integra universi orbis descriptio
creator: Oronce Fine
role_in_essay: The southern continent drawn as a coherent landmass on a map of the whole world.
notes: The canonical Terra Australis image for Act I. No holding copy, state or scan has been identified, so it is a candidate and not yet a usable object.

title: Nova et aucta orbis terrae descriptio ad usum navigantium emendate accommodata
creator: Gerardus Mercator
role_in_essay: The projection that fixes the southern continent into the working chart of navigators.
notes: Only a handful of copies survive and they are not identical. Act I must name the copy it reproduces or use a documented facsimile and say so.

title: Typus Orbis Terrarum
creator: Abraham Ortelius
edition_state: Plate state and issue not established
role_in_essay: The atlas world map through which Terra Australis reaches its widest audience.
notes: Ortelius reworked this plate repeatedly and the southern coast is not identical across states. The state matters to the argument and is not yet known.

title: Blaeu world map (comparator, exact object to be selected)
creator: Willem or Joan Blaeu
role_in_essay: A seventeenth-century comparator showing the southern coast after the Ortelius generation.
notes: Included only if it marks a distinct evidentiary stage. If it merely repeats Ortelius it should be dropped rather than shown as filler.

title: Coronelli terrestrial globe and printed gores
creator: Vincenzo Maria Coronelli
publication_context: Venice; printed gores issued for assembly
edition_state: Which gore set and issue is not established
scan_source: David Rumsey Historical Map Collection (blog record located, object record not opened)
role_in_essay: Coronelli's world in the round, and what its southern calotte does or does not show.
notes: A Rumsey record for the 1688 terrestrial globe was located by search during this audit; the catalogue entry itself was not retrieved. The southern calotte has not been examined, so Act III may not yet say what it depicts.

title: Terre Polari, Artiche, ed Antartiche
creator: Vincenzo Maria Coronelli
role_in_essay: The single object on which Act III's reading of Coronelli's polar geography rests.
notes: The Rumsey detail page returned an access check to this audit and its metadata could not be transcribed. Search results indicate the plate is dominated by the northern polar regions, which if true is itself the finding Act III should report; it is recorded here as unverified because the plate has not been seen.

title: Atlante Veneto polar material (exact plates to be identified)
creator: Vincenzo Maria Coronelli
role_in_essay: The publication context that shows the polar plates were part of a comprehensive world, not a curiosity.
notes: A placeholder for whatever the Atlante Veneto audit finds. It must resolve to named plates or be deleted; it may not stay a gesture at a thirteen-volume work.

title: A Chart of the Southern Hemisphere, according to the latest Discoveries with the Tracks of the Resolution, Captn Cook and the Adventure, Captn Furneaux, from 1772 to 1775
creator: William Whitchurch (engraver), after James Cook
publication_context: Issued with A Voyage towards the South Pole, London: Strahan and Cadell, 1777
edition_state: Etching as issued with the 1777 publication
role_in_essay: The hinge object of the whole essay: the tracks that bound the blank.
notes: Catalogue record read during this audit and the fields above transcribed from it. The record states no licence; it offers print sales and image licensing through RMG Images, so reproduction is research_only until terms are obtained in writing.

title: A chart of the Southern Hemisphere according to the latest discoveries: with the tracks of the Resolution, Capn Cook: and the Adventure Capn Furneaux from 1772 to 1775
creator: After James Cook
publication_context: Second Greenwich record of the same chart
role_in_essay: A second copy, held so the essay can say which copy it reproduces.
notes: Located by search; the record was not opened. Recorded because two Greenwich records for one chart is precisely the kind of ambiguity an object register exists to resolve.

title: Bellingshausen expedition chart material (exact plates to be identified)
creator: Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen
publication_context: Russian expedition atlas accompanying the published narrative
role_in_essay: What the 1819-21 voyage charted, as against what later writers say it saw.
notes: A named repository and plate list are required. The priority argument cannot be illustrated from a chart nobody has located.

title: Chart of the South Polar Sea (as issued with Weddell's Voyage)
creator: James Weddell
publication_context: A Voyage towards the South Pole, London, 1825
role_in_essay: An exceptional ice year charted as if it were the normal state of the sea.
notes: Title given here is the form usually cited and has not been checked against a copy.

title: Wilkes Antarctic chart material (exact sheets to be identified)
creator: Charles Wilkes
role_in_essay: Charted coast, some of which was later sailed through: the bridge from Act V into Act VI.
notes: This object carries the essay's most consequential ghost-geography claim, so it needs an exact sheet and an exact position before anything is said about it.

title: Ross south polar chart material (exact sheets to be identified)
creator: James Clark Ross
publication_context: Issued with A Voyage of Discovery and Research, London, 1847
role_in_essay: The first survey coast in the dataset that is drawn from sustained observation.
notes: Ross is the point at which the register must distinguish observed coast from reported coast on the same sheet.

title: Ice chart of the southern hemisphere compiled from the voyages of Cook 1772-5, Bellingshausen 1819-21, Weddell 1822-4, Foster 1828-9, Biscoe 1830-2, Balleny 1839, D'Urville 1839, Wilkes 1839, Ross 1841-2-3, Scott 1901-4, and Shackleton 1908-9
creator: United Kingdom Hydrographic Office; Carrington; Thomas Malby
edition_state: 1910 issue of a chart first compiled in 1874
dimensions: Printed area 29.5 cm diameter on sheet 855 x 680 mm
role_in_essay: The anchor object of Act VII: eleven voyages across 137 years compiled onto one sheet.
notes: Catalogue record read during this audit. Two facts from it change the argument: the credit line is Crown copyright, and the record dates the object 1910 and 1874, which means the 1910 sheet is itself a reissue of an earlier compilation. The layered archive is therefore literal.

title: Ice chart of the southern hemisphere compiled from the voyages of Cook 1772-5 ... and Ross 1841-2-3, from the papers on icebergs in the Southern Ocean by Towson 1855-59
creator: United Kingdom Hydrographic Office; Towson
role_in_essay: The 1910 chart's own predecessor, and the proof that cumulative charts are themselves revised.
notes: Located by search; record not opened. If the 1874 and 1910 sheets can be compared, Act VII gains its best single demonstration that a synthesis is a dated state and not a summary of everything known.

title: Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition plan chart (exact object to be identified)
creator: Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition
role_in_essay: The planned crossing, which Act VIII fades to background once the drift begins.
notes: The plan has to come from a dated object rather than from a modern redrawing, or the contrast between plan and drift is a contrast between two of our own graphics.

title: Worsley drift and boat-journey chart material (exact object to be identified)
creator: Frank Arthur Worsley
publication_context: Expedition navigational records and published accounts
role_in_essay: The navigator's own record, which is the only thing that can separate a fix from an interpolation.
notes: The single most important unresolved object in the programme. Until it is located, every Endurance position in the dataset is taken from a published narrative and must be labelled as such.
